ORDER Heard on the question of admission.

This miscellaneous petition under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereafter referred to as the Code) has been directed against impugned order dated 17.02.2025 (Annexure P/1)
passed in Sessions Trial No.06 of 2021 by learned Seventh Additional Sessions Judge, Bhind,
District Bhind (MP), whereby an application dated 17.02.2025 (Annexure P/3) filed on behalf of the petitioner under Section 233 of the Code = Section 256 (3) of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhiya,
2023 (BNSS, 2023) has been rejected.

2. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the victim has eloped several times after the date of incident in the present case, which is based on First Information Report (FIR)
which was lodged after a delay of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:5913 2 MCRC-10773-2025 seven months.

He further submits that to prove the conduct of the victim, he has made a request to call Mukesh Garg and H.C.M., Police Station Rural Kotwali Bhind, District Bhind (MP) to prove conduct of the victim, but his application has been dismissed only on the ground that no evidence can be adduced impeaching bad conduct of the victim.
3. Learned counsel submits that the impugned order is bad in law, as present case vide First Information Report No.0687 dated 17.11.2019 (Annexure P/2) has been filed under Sections 376 (D)
and 366 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC), therefore, urges this Court for allowing the present petition by setting aside the impugned order.

sentences.text: 4. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and perused the impugned order along with the documents / material made available on record.

5. To appreciate the controversy involved in the present matter, Section 54 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 is relevant and extracted, as under: -
"54.
Previous bad character not relevant, except in reply.

-- In criminal proceedings,
the fact that the accused person has a bad character, is irrelevant, unless evidence has been given that he has a good character, in which case it becomes relevant.

Explanation 1. -- This section does not apply to cases in which the bad character of any person is itself a fact in issue.
Explanation 2. -- A previous conviction is relevant as evidence of bad character."
6. It is not in dispute that in present case, FIR has been lodged against the petitioner under Sections 376 (D) and 366 of IPC.
It is also not in dispute that bad character and conduct of the victim cannot be put to test unless evidence has been adduced with regard to good character of the victim.
In NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:5913 3 MCRC-10773-2025 such a situation, her previous character is neither relevant nor in issue.
The same view has been taken by the learned trial Court for dismissing the application.
This Court does not find any illegality or infirmity in the impugned order, therefore, not inclined to interfere with the aforesaid order.
7. The present petition being sans merit, fails and is hereby dismissed.
Pending interlocutory application, if any, also stands disposed off.

(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE Adnan Awdesh @ Parua Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196997386/
